# Conformance Requirements Checklist: Provider Conformance, Compatibility and Composition

**Purpose**: Standard-depth requirements-quality review of reusable category agreements, composition, compatibility and contributor scope before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-10-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)
**Audience / timing**: Maintainers and provider-contract reviewers during draft PR review, before implementation authorization.

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and the maintainer's request for an assisted assessment.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is reviewer-owned. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means requirements-quality approval, not implementation completion. Generation and the assessment below do not set approval markers.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the versioned inventory's authority, mandatory guarantees, optional extensions and environmental exclusions explicitly defined without redefining predecessor contracts? [Completeness, Spec FR-001..003]
- [ ] CHK002 Are unchanged consumers and expectations required for both independent metadata and both independent artifact options, with provider-specific bindings limited to setup, faults and observations? [Completeness, Spec FR-002..005]
- [ ] CHK003 Are inherited metadata guarantees, including uncertain outcomes, schema, backup/restore and actual durable recovery, explicitly retained? [Completeness, Spec FR-004]
- [ ] CHK004 Are artifact visibility, verification, protected reads, shared deletion authority, incarnation fencing and interrupted-work guarantees explicitly retained without assuming rename or cross-store transactions? [Completeness, Spec FR-005]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the distinction between common logical conformance, durable-local evidence, object simulation and undeveloped operational categories unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec FR-003, FR-023]
- [ ] CHK006 Is applicability defined so a missing mandatory fault binding or changed capability cannot remove a logical guarantee from the expected inventory? [Clarity, Spec FR-001..002, FR-018, FR-020]
- [ ] CHK007 Are the finite baseline/replacement compositions and each rejected subvariant specified rather than described as unrestricted provider permutations? [Clarity, Spec FR-006..008, FR-014]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 Are optional-target requirements consistent across absent, registered-disabled, enabled-compatible and enabled-incompatible cases, with no fallback or capability granted by unavailable targets? [Consistency, Spec FR-008, FR-010]
- [ ] CHK009 Are permitted protocol/identity multiplicity and authoritative metadata/artifact singleton rules consistent with disabled-module and route-ownership requirements? [Consistency, Spec FR-007..008]
- [ ] CHK010 Do initialization, readiness, cancellation and shutdown requirements distinguish finite observation from actual settlement without implying release of non-cooperative work? [Consistency, Spec FR-009, FR-016, SC-007]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK011 Are inherited category entries and parameterized subproof obligations enumerated sufficiently to measure complete applicable coverage rather than rely on totals? [Measurability, Spec SC-001, FR-018, FR-020]
- [ ] CHK012 Are large-transfer size, incremental memory and real interruption/recovery criteria stated separately from outer observation budgets and simulated evidence? [Measurability, Spec FR-005, SC-004, SC-007]
- [ ] CHK013 Are red/green acceptance requirements explicit about the intended assertion failure, unchanged expected guarantee and corrected counterpart, excluding incidental setup failure? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec FR-019, SC-003, SC-005]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 Are invalid declarations, dependency cycles, capability gaps, cardinality and route conflicts covered with preconstruction rejection and valid repairs? [Coverage, Spec FR-007, FR-019, US2 scenarios 2,5]
- [ ] CHK015 Are disabled effects, failed recovery, cancellation, non-cooperative initialization/cleanup and explicit settled restart addressed without adding hot replacement? [Coverage, Spec FR-006, FR-008..009, US2 scenarios 1,3,4]
- [ ] CHK016 Are version boundaries, malformed declarations, prerelease flags and independent host/abstraction/dependency axes documented under the existing policy? [Edge Cases, Spec FR-010..011, US3 scenario 1]
- [ ] CHK017 Are unchanged-source and retained-old-binary requirements distinct, with attributable immutable baselines and deliberate breaks that cannot be replaced by recompilation? [Coverage, Spec FR-012, US3 scenarios 2,3]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK018 Are prohibited direct/transitive/public-contract coupling and permitted integration counterparts specified without making the test SDK a production dependency? [Dependency, Spec FR-013, Plan Project Structure]
- [ ] CHK019 Are contributor prerequisites, independent packaging, good/faulty examples and correction-only boundaries defined without claiming the forwarding example is another independent provider? [Completeness, Spec FR-015, FR-024, SC-005]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK020 Are exclusions and unsupported combinations explicit enough to prevent technical fixture qualification being read as production support, protocol/identity operations, native-client certification or release authority? [Clarity, Spec FR-014, FR-023..024, Assumptions]

## Assisted Assessment

The maintainer requested assessment as well as generation. All 20 criteria have
supporting written requirements; no unresolved requirements-quality blocker or
product decision was identified. This is an advisory assessment, not reviewer
approval, runtime evidence or implementation authorization. All markers remain
unchecked for the reviewer.

| CHK007..010,014..015 | [Matrix: Fixture-Host Compositions, CP-01..20](../contracts/matrix.md); [harness: Finite Work and Isolation](../contracts/harness.md); [acceptance QC-13..21](../contracts/acceptance.md) |

| CHK016..018 | [Matrix: Version/Policy Expansion / Source, Binary and Architecture Inventory](../contracts/matrix.md); [plan: Project Structure](../plan.md); [acceptance QC-22..28](../contracts/acceptance.md) |
| CHK019..020 | [Harness: Contributor Entry Point](../contracts/harness.md); [matrix: Unsupported Choices and Reporting](../contracts/matrix.md); [quickstart](../quickstart.md); [acceptance QC-29..32,37,47](../contracts/acceptance.md) |

Implementation watch-outs, not missing requirements: preserve every inherited
assertion/subproof while extracting independent bindings; freeze old consumers
before candidate execution; actually perform the 256 MiB/4 GiB transfers and
SQLite/Local crash proofs. None can be satisfied by a generated inventory.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after reviewer approval of requirements quality.
- Leave unresolved or unevaluated items unchecked; record findings inline.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- IDs are sequential within this file; cite the filename with an ID.
